_comment: fixtureِ مصنوعیِ G.6 (گامِ «سنجه‌شده با fixture»). هیچ عددی از دستگاه واقعی نیست: سمتِ exporter = tests/fixtures/exporter_response_*.txt (دو module، همان فایل‌های G.5.1) و سمتِ snapshot = ساختارِ collect_hp/collect_canon با همان اعدادِ خودسازگارِ کامنت‌دارِ آن فایل‌ها (12345 − 1200 = 11145، 9245678 tick → 1d 01:40، 1344/3200 → 42٪). پس pair_ok «خودمقصد» نیست: مسیرِ ترجمه (آینه) و مسیرِ نام‌گذاریِ snapshot دو کدِ جدا هستند و ابزار باید آن‌ها را به هم برساند. عددِ واقعیِ PDU و اختلافِ واقعیِ دو منبع روی سرورِ مالک سنجیده می‌شود — در repo ثبت نمی‌شود.
exporter_capture:
# PrintGuard fixture — synthetic, hand-written (گام G.5.1)
#
# What this file is: the Prometheus exposition text that `snmp_exporter` 0.26.0 is
# expected to return for one module-scrape of a mono HP LaserJet:
#
#     GET /snmp?target=172.16.0.5&module=printer_hp&auth=public_v2
#
# What this file is NOT: a capture. No exporter was run anywhere in this phase (the
# phase rules forbid downloading the binary and running real SNMP), so every number and
# every string below was chosen by hand from `monitoring/snmp.yml` (module printer_hp:
# 14 metrics) and is labelled accordingly in tests. Treat it as a *format* fixture:
# the shapes it pins are the ones derived from the exporter source in this session —
#   * a metric name is exactly the `name:` field of snmp.yml — no `printer_hp_` prefix;
#   * text-valued metrics (DisplayString) carry the value in a label named after the
#     metric and value 1 (collector.go: "For strings we put the value as a label with the
#     same name as the metric", value = 1.0);
#   * the five self-metrics carry the const label module="printer_hp"
#     (collector.go: moduleLabel) and NO `instance` label — 0.26.0 adds no instance
#     label of its own (grep for "instance" in collector.go and main.go: 0 hits);
#   * a value of -2/-3 on a metric whose snmp.yml entry has `# ignore_values:` is the
#     "device does not report this" sentinel, not a measurement.
#
# hp_fax is deliberately absent (printer has no fax) and general_oids / hp_npcl_pct_oid
# deliberately carry sentinels, so the missing-sentinel paths are exercised too.
# TYPE snmp_scrape_duration_seconds gauge
# HELP snmp_scrape_duration_seconds Total SNMP time scrape took (walk and processing).
snmp_scrape_duration_seconds{module="printer_hp"} 0.0153
# TYPE snmp_scrape_walk_duration_seconds gauge
snmp_scrape_walk_duration_seconds{module="printer_hp"} 0.0121
# TYPE snmp_scrape_packets_sent gauge
snmp_scrape_packets_sent{module="printer_hp"} 3
# TYPE snmp_scrape_packets_retried gauge
snmp_scrape_packets_retried{module="printer_hp"} 0
# TYPE snmp_scrape_pdus_returned gauge
snmp_scrape_pdus_returned{module="printer_hp"} 14
# TYPE hp_model gauge
# HELP hp_model PrintGuard printer_hp: hp_model [core/oid/catalog.py:22]
hp_model{hp_model="HP LaserJet Pro M402dn"} 1
# TYPE hp_serial gauge
hp_serial{hp_serial="CNCVC0245A"} 1
# TYPE hp_firmware gauge
hp_firmware{hp_firmware="20190418"} 1
# TYPE general_oids_2 gauge
general_oids_2 12
# TYPE hp_scan_color counter
hp_scan_color 400
# TYPE hp_print_color counter
hp_print_color 1200
# TYPE hp_copy_color counter
hp_copy_color 30
# TYPE hp_copy_mono counter
hp_copy_mono 900
# TYPE hp_scan_mono counter
hp_scan_mono 60
# TYPE candidate_subtrees_hp gauge
candidate_subtrees_hp{candidate_subtrees_hp="4.1.11.2.3.9.4.2.1.1"} 1
# TYPE candidate_subtrees_hp_2 gauge
candidate_subtrees_hp_2{candidate_subtrees_hp_2="4.1.11.2.3.9.4.2.1.4"} 1
# TYPE general_oids gauge
general_oids -2
# TYPE hp_npcl_pct_oid gauge
hp_npcl_pct_oid -3

# PrintGuard fixture — synthetic, hand-written (گام G.5.1)
#
# Expected response of the second module-scrape for the same mono HP device:
#
#     GET /snmp?target=172.16.0.5&module=printer_std&auth=public_v2
#
# Same caveats as exporter_response_sample.txt: not a capture. Shapes follow
# `monitoring/snmp.yml` (module printer_std: 24 metrics — 11 get, 2 walk roots).
#
# Why this file exists: `printer_hp` has no toner, tray, cover or sys_* metric, so the
# HP shape (toners/trays/alerts/uptime) can only be assembled from the standard MIB
# module. The numbers are deliberately self-consistent with the hp fixture:
#   bro_total 12345 − bro_color 1200 = 11145 = bw_std = bro_bw
#   sys_uptime 9245678 ticks (1/100 s) → 92456 s → "1d 01:40"
#   toner_remain_1 1344 / toner_max_1 3200 → 42 % → status ok
#   tray1_level 130 / tray1_cap 250 → 52 % → status medium
#   tray2_level −3 → empty (and −3 is an ignore_values sentinel on this metric, so the
#   dropped value falls back to the collector default −9, which is also "empty")
#   toner_remain_2 −2 → level None / status unknown (ignored sentinel ⇒ same result)
#   cover_status 4 → no alert (4 = closed)
# toner_name_2 is "Imaging Drum", which no colour keyword matches: it must land on the
# generic toner_2 key, exactly like _hp_toner_key() in core/collectors/hp.py decides.
# TYPE sys_descr gauge
# HELP sys_descr PrintGuard printer_std: sys_descr [core/oid/catalog.py:8]
sys_descr{sys_descr="HP HP LaserJet Pro M402dn  Series:V6.05.10  (lua)"} 1
# TYPE sys_object_id gauge
sys_object_id{sys_object_id="1.3.6.1.4.1.11.5.3.8.1"} 1
# TYPE sys_uptime gauge
sys_uptime 9245678
# TYPE sys_hostname gauge
sys_hostname{sys_hostname="hp-m402-05"} 1
# TYPE model_mib gauge
model_mib{model_mib="HP LaserJet Pro M402dn"} 1
# TYPE serial_mib gauge
serial_mib{serial_mib="CNCVC0245A"} 1
# TYPE cover_status gauge
cover_status 4
# TYPE bro_total counter
bro_total 12345
# TYPE bro_color counter
bro_color 1200
# TYPE bw_std counter
bw_std 11145
# TYPE bro_bw counter
bro_bw 11145
# TYPE standard gauge
standard{standard="Ordinary"} 1
# TYPE toner_name_1 gauge
toner_name_1{toner_name_1="Black Toner"} 1
# TYPE toner_max_1 gauge
toner_max_1 3200
# TYPE toner_remain_1 gauge
toner_remain_1 1344
# TYPE toner_name_2 gauge
toner_name_2{toner_name_2="Imaging Drum"} 1
# TYPE toner_max_2 gauge
toner_max_2 100
# TYPE toner_remain_2 gauge
toner_remain_2 -2
# TYPE tray1_cap gauge
tray1_cap 250
# TYPE tray1_level gauge
tray1_level 130
# TYPE tray1_name gauge
tray1_name{tray1_name="Tray 1"} 1
# TYPE tray2_cap gauge
tray2_cap 150
# TYPE tray2_level gauge
tray2_level -3
# TYPE tray2_name gauge
tray2_name{tray2_name="Manual Feed Tray"} 1
